# Epistle of Barnabas — Chapter 12 (EMET Literal)

**Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Epistle of Barnabas 12
**Agent:** EMET (Literal)
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

1. Similarly concerning the cross he says again in Moses, when Israel was being warred upon by foreigners, and in order to remind those being warred upon that they had been handed over to death because of their sins — the Spirit speaks to the heart of Moses to make a type of the cross and of him who is to suffer, because, he says, unless they trust in him, war shall prevail over them forever.
2. Moses therefore placed one weapon upon another in the midst of the encounter, and standing higher than all of them he stretched out his hands, and in this way Israel again prevailed; and then whenever he put his hands down they began to perish.
3. Why? So that they might know that they were unable to be saved if they did not hope in him.
4. And again in another prophet he says: "All day long I stretched out my hands to a disobedient people who contradicted my righteous way."
5. And again Moses makes a type of Jesus, showing that he must suffer and himself give life, although they will believe that they have destroyed him — by the sign of the serpent being made as they fell by the serpent. For the Lord placed it to show them: "Shall everyone who is bitten by the serpent, looking upon it, be saved?" — seeing that in a serpent there is no salvation.
6. Yes, and again he has glory in the midst of these types: for the Father says to the Son: "Let us make the human being according to our image and likeness, and let them rule over the beasts of the earth and the birds of the air and the fish of the sea." And when the Lord saw the beautiful creation, he said, "Increase and multiply and fill the earth." These things were said to the Son.
7. I will also show you how he speaks to us. He made a second creation in these last days. And the Lord says: "Behold, I make the last things as the first." The prophet therefore said that he preached to those who had perished in the sea, and to those in the deep, and to those of Sheol.
8. And further he says: "And there came from the mountains of Israel a shoot and it grew and became great." The shoot is David, and the mountains of Israel are the tribes of Israel.
9. And again: "In the last days the mountain of the Lord shall be revealed and the house of God." — This is the coming of our Lord.
